fact: The Kenya Space Agency says Kenya launched the CroME Initiative with the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development, Microsoft AI for Good Lab and NASA Harvest, using satellite images and AI to provide crop maps, crop growth monitoring, yield predictions and crop damage detection.

NASA Harvest's Catherine Nakalembe says she set out to map crop types in western Kenya using satellite image data, and uses machine learning to map cropland, classify crop types and estimate yields in Kenya and other African countries.

The ADM-Kenya final report states that the project, co-developed with the Ministry of Agriculture, icipe and RCMRD, delivered four satellite-based drought and crop condition products fed into the RCMRD and icipe geoportals, and the ministry plans to include them in its monthly Food Security and Agricultural Status Bulletin.

The State Department for Livestock Development says its Kenya Livestock Insurance Program uses satellite-derived NDVI forage availability to decide payouts in arid and semi-arid counties, with cover implemented by the State Department and county governments.
The State Department for Livestock Development says KLIP has covered 100,000 people in six years, with payouts of KSh 1.3 billion.

Kenya's National Drought Management Authority says it operates the Drought Early Warning System, which uses satellite imagery with ground stations to monitor rainfall, temperature and soil moisture and warn of drought.
NDMA says it publishes monthly drought early warning bulletins giving drought status, drawing on satellite imagery among other data.
